text:
rhea: Noticed a weird failure while onboarding Meridian's LoRA adapter (cust-meridian). After stitch-merge + int4 quant, long-form outputs start repeating a short clause and then append an unrelated policy footer. cc @mike @noor

mike: Huh. Repetition + appended footer sounds like attention routing or stop-token detection problem. Any logs or example outputs?

rhea: Example (fp16 merged):
User: Write a 6-step onboarding checklist for new delivery drivers.
Assistant (fp16): Step 1... Step 6: confirm training.
Assistant (int4 merged): Step 1... Step 3... Step 3... Step 3... [REPEATED] 
-- Privacy policy: This service may log...

noor: The privacy policy footer is not part of the prompt. Could be a cookie text stuck in a cached KV prefix or a misrouted persona token mapped to a footer template id.

eli: Any warnings during merge or runtime? Kernel fallbacks? KV-cache warnings?

rhea: CI quickpack summary: PASS 78, FAIL 22. Failures clustered: repetition-loop (10), unexpected-footer (7), numeric-deltas (5). Quick repro command I ran:
```bash
./eval_quickpack.sh --customer meridian --adapter meridian-lora-v1 \
  --merge stitch --quant int4 --suites instruction,longform,regress --seed 99
# metrics: rep_loop_rate:0.10 -> 0.27; avg_resp_len +8% (because footer appended)
```

mike: I pulled a short trace. There's a repeated attention-mask warning: "attn_head_permute_mismatch" during the merged adapter forward when using int4 kernels. Not seen on fp16 baseline. Could be a head reordering quirk introduced by merge metadata and the quant pack expects canonical head order.

noor: If head indices are permuted, KV indices could point to stale prefix fragments, explaining cached footer injection and token repetition if the model attends to an unintended prefix.

eli: Proposed triage steps:
1) Run forward with --dump-attn-head-map on base, adapter, merged to compare head index maps.
2) Re-merge using "preserve-head-order" flag (if adapter metadata allows).
3) Run quant-pack with "verify-head-alignment" to catch permutes during kernel packing.
4) Run prefix-only baseline (disable kv-cache reuse) to confirm whether footer comes from cache vs tokenizer.

rhea: I'll run step 1 & 4 now and upload traces to /shared/evals/meridian/traces.tar.gz.

mike: If preserve-head-order fixes it, we should patch the merge service to align attention-head metadata and add a CI validation that compares head maps post-merge.

ci-bot: /ci/11011: merge-smoke triggered by @rhea. Added probe: dump-attn-head-map enabled. Results will post to /ci/11011/logs.

noor: Small quick hack to test: remerge with adapter-rescale=0.7 and pack with verify-head-alignment=true. If repetition drops, we have good signal.

rhea: I ran prefix-only inference (kv_cache disabled): repetition rate dropped to 0.12 and footer disappeared. Looks strongly cache-related. Uploading per-example diffs.

mike: Strong signal that a KV-cache index mismatch is causing the model to attend to a leftover footer prefix from some internal test harness. Next steps: 1) repro with preserve-head-order, 2) add head-map verification in packer, 3) scrub leftover static prefixes in canary infra.

eli: I'll start a GH issue with traces + suggested guard rails: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/4699. Attaching attn maps and kv indices.

rhea: Thanks all. If preserve-head-order + verify-head-alignment passes on CI sweep, we'll push a canary for Meridian pinned to int4 with the guard rails. Otherwise fallback = serve fp16 merged for that account.

mike: Copy. Will follow-up on merge-service patch.

rhea: Closing for now; will post CI sweep results here when done. :white_check_mark:
